about: The interim register of the engine seam (geom_op::engine::Engine, which programs reach through engine-geometry): one row for each operation of the trait and each case of its inputs that a different part answers, saying what answers it today in geom-solidcore's engine (SolidcoreEngine), the test of tests/engine.rs that pins today's answer, its known faults (ids of tests/named-faults.json), the tolerance it works to, and the kernel piece or chapter that will make it exact. Where the kernel's own exact operation answers a case, it does; solidcore answers only what the kernel cannot yet. case and answered_by are word for word what the engine's edition says. tests/engine.rs fails while an operation of the trait has no row here, a row names a test or fault that does not exist, or the edition answers otherwise. Every lane that adds an operation to the trait, or moves a case to another engine, adds or changes its row here. programs holds the interim places on a program's side of the seam: the place, what answers it today, the file and test that pin today's behaviour, its known faults, and what replaces it; the program's own test (for Spare Construct, the server's tests/kernel.rs) fails while a row names a file or test that does not exist.

operations.answered_by: geom-solidcore's own record: the engine's name, solidcore's repository and pinned commit, the grid step, solidcore's default tolerances and the answers below
operations.tolerance: none: it reports, it does not compute
operations.exact_by: stays: an exact engine of the kernel's own gives its own edition (chapter 26, versions and editions)

operations.case: a profile with no holes, level, swept straight up, which make.prism takes (strictly convex)
operations.tolerance: exact: the kernel's own prism on the grid

operations.case: every other profile: holes, a profile not level or not swept straight up, or one make.prism refuses
known_faults: SC-8
operations.tolerance: solidcore's zone of 1e-5 m (0.01 mm); the body is converted to the grid, each flat face's plane written through its own grid corners, recorded Certified within that and a step, and checked by geom-check at its full level
operations.exact_by: geom-sweep's Extrude (chapter 13.4) on the kernel's exact grid; until then a profile with a round hole stays refused (SC-8)

operations.tolerance: exact: the arrangement of flat faces adds no error, and the result is as exact as the least exact operand
operations.exact_by: already the kernel's exact geom-bool (chapter 11); curved operands wait for chapter 11's certified curved booleans

operations.tolerance: exact: the arrangement of flat faces adds no error, and each piece is as exact as the least exact operand
operations.recorded: the selection is every cell inside the target and outside the tool (geom-bool's cells), each piece one solid checked by geom-check at its full level, ordered by its vertices' grid points sorted by x, then y, then z: a strip cut in two by a box across it gives its first and last 8 m in that order (where subtract gives one solid of two shells), and a box across the whole strip gives no piece (a_strip_cut_in_two_leaves_two_pieces_in_order)

operations.case: sections whose walls are flat: each wall's four corners on one plane
operations.answered_by: the engine's own rows: each wall and each end one flat face through the sections' grid corners, Exact
operations.tolerance: exact: every corner is the caller's grid point and every face the plane through its own grid corners, so nothing is rounded; the body is recorded Exact and checked by geom-check at its full level
operations.recorded: each wall between two sections and each end is its own flat face, however little a wall turns from its neighbours, also where two walls lie in one plane (a later boolean merges those): a loft of three sections 500 mm apart whose walls bend by 0.46 degrees, by none and by 1.15 degrees is one closed solid of 10 faces and the closed form's volume each time (a_loft_whose_walls_bend_less_than_half_a_degree_is_one_face_per_wall), as is a strip over ground uneven by a few millimetres through eleven sections (a_loft_over_uneven_ground_is_its_profile_times_its_length), and a section two of whose sides turn by 0.05 degrees lofts to one face per side (a_section_whose_sides_turn_less_than_half_a_degree_lofts_to_one_face_per_side); the same loft gives the same bytes (the_same_loft_gives_the_same_bytes). solidcore's skin is not used: at the pin it joins neighbouring walls that turn by less than half a degree, across sections or between two sides of a section, into one bent B-spline face the kernel has no kind for (its continuity tests' CONTINUITY_ANGLE, a constant no caller sets; a replay of a real site's envelope found it for every loft of more than two stations and every strip of a void whose last side is carried on along its slope). A section not wholly ahead of the one before it is an invalid input (a_loft_that_folds_back_is_a_fault_not_a_solid); a loft whose walls cross (a section half a turn round) is refused as it is written, each crossed wall's halves cancelling to no area (a_crossed_loft_is_refused_for_walls_with_no_area), and the kernel's checker, which every result passes, refuses any other body whose faces cross. A wall that is not flat is unsupported (a_loft_wall_that_is_not_flat_is_unsupported): the kernel has no kind for a ruled surface yet. Sections of different corner counts are refused: the caller pairs the corners
operations.exact_by: geom-sweep's ruled loft (chapter 13.6): one face per matched edge pair, a plane where its four corners are coplanar by an exact orient3d test, so the loft is Exact; ruled faces otherwise, Certified

operations.tolerance: exact: the arrangement of flat faces adds no error, and the result's bound is the operands' combined
operations.recorded: no retry, heal or nudge. Two strips sharing a face exactly unite into one solid with the face count of the whole strip. At slivers of 0.5, 1 and 3 mm (the second strip raised by the sliver, overlapping by it, or apart by it) every union is a closed body of the closed form's volume: one shell when raised or overlapping, two shells when apart, the gap kept exactly as wide (the_sliver_unions_are_as_recorded). Two solids that touch only along an edge, as two envelopes cut at a corner of a site meet along its vertical line, or only at a point, have no solid union: geom-bool makes the exact non-manifold body (of the kind General) and the engine refuses it, naming the edges where more than two faces meet or the point (a_union_of_solids_touching_only_along_an_edge_or_at_a_point_is_refused_by_name; a replay of a real site's ten cut envelopes found it for four unions, each pair touching along one vertical edge)

operations.tolerance: solidcore's zone of 1e-5 m (0.01 mm), merging faces closer than it (SC-1's cause); the result converted and checked by geom-check at its full level
operations.recorded: a cylinder standing on a swept box is united by solidcore and the result refused by the kernel's checker, which has no certified test yet of the pairs the circle's arcs make (engine.rs module test a_curved_solid_is_united_by_solidcore); a curved solid with one solidcore holds no body of (made by the kernel's prism or geom-bool) is unsupported (a_curved_solid_with_a_kernel_made_one_is_unsupported). No solid the seam makes today has a curved face: extrude takes polygons and loft refuses walls that are not flat
operations.exact_by: chapter 11's certified curved booleans (geom-bool), after geom-check's certified tests of arcs (CK-3)

operations.case: a flat-faced solid and a plane square to a grid axis
operations.answered_by: the kernel's geom-bool prepare and geom-poly local_cuts and section, joined into loops by geom-solidcore
operations.tolerance: exact: every point the meeting of three planes the solid and the cut hold, as a fraction of steps in lowest terms; the cut carries the solid's exactness
operations.recorded: geom-solidcore's own code (src/cut.rs) decides from the solid's corners whether the plane misses or only touches it (no loops), names each edge's face by its plane (the carrier, normal out of the solid), turns each edge with the material on its left seen from the plane's normal, joins the edges into loops one edge per face in a row, checks each closed and orders them from their least points. Unsupported, as values: a curved face, a plane not square to a grid axis, a corner of the solid on the plane (chapter 18.4's tie rules: a face in the plane is never a cut, touching loops at a saddle), a point where more than two edges of the cut meet, a point whose exact fraction does not fit 128 bits (a_plane_the_engine_does_not_cut_yet_is_a_value). solidcore's plane section (Modeller::plane_section) is not the answer: it cuts only the solids solidcore made (the kernel's prism and geom-bool keep no solidcore body), its curves are doubles and name no face; it is the oracle on the walls solidcore's sweep makes, agreeing within a step (the_cut_agrees_with_solidcore_s_plane_section). Pull request 1041 (WR-1, a plane on no grid) is not on main and does not bite a plane square to a grid axis
operations.exact_by: the kernel's exact sections of every body kind (piece G389, chapter 18.4), with the tie rules; then Spare Construct's plans read it through the same trait (note A12, build-order step 3)
